title: The Ford Extended Warranty Scam What Finance Managers Hide!
summary: A finance-office exposé walks through ten dealership tactics used to oversell, mark up, and obscure extended warranty terms.

assertions.quote: that markup is frequently 50% or more above what the dealership paid
it is just as negotiable as anything else on that contract
you are now financing that warranty over five or six years at whatever interest rate your loan carries
you can purchase a service contract weeks or even months after the original sale

verdicts.note: Most manufacturer and many third-party extended plans can be bought any time before factory coverage lapses, not only at the point of sale.

assertions.quote: many dealerships also sell third-party warranty contracts from outside companies that may offer higher commissions to the dealership

verdicts.note: Third-party administrators vary widely in reputation and claims practices compared to manufacturer-backed plans, a distinction regularly flagged by consumer advocates.

assertions.quote: Finance managers rarely walk through this exclusion list line by line

verdicts.note: Sales presentations emphasizing coverage while skipping exclusions are a frequently reported F&I sales practice, though not universal.

assertions.quote: any sign of a prior issue, even something completely unrelated to the current repair, becomes grounds to argue the problem was pre-existing

verdicts.note: Pre-existing-condition denials do get stretched to marginal or unrelated findings in some disputes, but 'any sign' overstates how routinely this specific tactic is used.

assertions.quote: the process to actually get that refund is often made deliberately frustrating

verdicts.note: The lengthy multi-step process is widely reported by consumers; whether it is deliberately designed to discourage cancellation versus merely bureaucratic isn't independently provable.

CFPB found servicers "abusively required consumers to make two separate in-person dealership visits to cancel" an otherwise-cancelable, pro-rata-refundable product -- a burdensome process, though not the specific forms/notarization/odometer-statement steps the claim lists.
